changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace deals, make this an explicit invitation rather than a claim: "Have one of your engineers build a working sitter-pay flow in our sandbox this weekend, and show it at Monday standup." Adapt the flow name to the buyer's own term for what they pay out.
changes.why: The rep places the turn from bake-off to commitment at the moment an engineer "built a working sitter payment flow over a weekend" on our docs and sandbox, and Daniel "stopped saying "if."" after that, so the proof was the build, not our claim.

changes.change: For marketplaces evaluating against Braintree, add a ready 'What you keep' proof point covering PayPal, Venmo and saved cards: a documented position on each, plus a named saved-card migration reference at comparable size. Fill it only with what solutions engineering confirms; do not publish until the Venmo answer exists.
changes.why: The customer's questions shifted to "Do we lose PayPal, do we lose Venmo, what happens to the saved cards", the rep had no "crisp answer on Venmo" and never sent the promised reference, and the customer's engineer still expects to "find out" during implementation.

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For sitter and service-provider apps: "Onboard, verify and pay your sitters in their local currency, so your engineers can stop babysitting payments." Say "sitter pay" and "the app", not "marketplace" or "payouts". Do not promise a pay-timing change (such as Friday pay) until we know how the CFO's timing question was answered.
changes.why: The onboarding, identity-check and local-currency capabilities landed, but the customer says "sitter pay" rather than "payouts" and frames the problem as toil ("We want to stop babysitting this.", "Payments shouldn't be a team"), with about two engineers kept on upkeep.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For small-ticket marketplaces, stop leading with the acceptance-rate slide. Keep it available only if the buyer raises authorization rates themselves.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide drew silence, and the buyer said "our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates."
